For a plain ndarray this was harmless, but when a **complex `NumpyExtensionArray`** is passed (as happens when the array isn't unboxed to a plain ndarray), it flowed straight into the Cython hashtable functions and raised `TypeError: No matching signature found`. This broke `duplicated()` for complex dtype (requirement #4). Every sibling branch (int, float) correctly does `np.asarray(values)`; the complex branch was simply inconsistent.
